term: elenctic defense of a first principle
definition: In Metaphysics IV.4,1006a11–28, Aristotle distinguishes demonstration from an elenctic showing whose starting concession is that the interlocutor signify something to himself and another. Determinate signification is extracted from that concession; the opponent who submits is responsible for the premise. This records the proposed dialectical method, not an automatically successful proof of every proposition indispensable to an inquiry, and not a universal epistemic-to-ontic bridge.
